findings.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key); the only call site orders by -datetime so the key is a datetime object, causing build_cursor to raise TypeError on any non-empty page (DateTimePaginator converts to a float timestamp first; this class skips that), so the optimized path 500s on the first request that returns rows

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:843 — value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value, which build_queryset then uses in datetime__lte=<int> / datetime__gte=<int>; any follow-up page with a non-zero cursor value produces an invalid DateTimeField lookup and errors

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access is evaluated unconditionally before the use_optimized check; organization_context.member is None for non-member authenticated requests (org auth tokens, integration/sentry-app tokens, staff without membership), so this raises AttributeError and breaks the existing endpoint for those callers even when optimized_pagination is not passed

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — In BasePaginator.get_result, a negative cursor.offset with is_prev set is passed straight into queryset[start_offset:stop]; Django QuerySets reject negative slicing (ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported), so a crafted prev cursor with a negative offset produces a 500; the comment claiming the underlying queryset handles boundary conditions is false, and this affects every paginator inheriting from BasePaginator

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:876 — The advanced negative-offset branch in OptimizedCursorPaginator calls list(queryset[negative:stop]), which raises in the Django ORM; the comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing automatically is incorrect, so the feature the class exists for cannot execute

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — The gate uses request.user.is_superuser (the account flag) instead of is_active_superuser(request), granting advanced mode to superuser accounts without an active elevated superuser session; additionally, the branch's stated goal of enabling access to data beyond normal pagination bounds via a hidden query parameter is a bypass-shaped design that should not be merged (a real reverse-pagination need belongs in the cursor protocol, not a superuser-only escape hatch)

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:820 — No tests cover OptimizedCursorPaginator, the new endpoint branch, or the changed negative-offset handling in BasePaginator.get_result; a single test requesting one page through the new path would have caught the failures

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:67 — optimized_pagination is a new query parameter on a public, documented endpoint but is not added to the endpoint's schema/parameters or docs, and its behavior differs per caller (silently ignored for non-admins)

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:820 — The docstring and PR description claim performance optimizations (optimized query path for large datasets, without full dataset scanning), but get_result is a near-verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result issuing the same query; there is no performance change and the class is duplicated code with a misleading name

src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26 — The added comment says negative offsets are now allowed as a performance optimization, but no code changed here (int(offset) already accepted negatives) and negative offsets are not supported downstream; the comment documents behavior that does not exist

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:843 — value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value, which build_queryset then uses in datetime__lte=<int> / datetime__gte=<int>; any follow-up page with a non-zero cursor value produces an invalid DateTimeField lookup and errors

adjudication.rationale: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is wired into `organization_auditlogs.py` with `order_by="-datetime"`, but its cursor/key handling is numeric: `get_item_key()` applies `math.floor/ceil` and returns an `int`, and `value_from_cursor()` returns `cursor.value` unchanged. For a datetime-ordered queryset, follow-up cursors will carry a non-zero numeric value that `build_queryset(...)` (inherited from `BasePaginator`) will use to construct filters against the ordering field (here `datetime`). That creates a type mismatch (datetime field compared to an `int`) and/or breaks when deriving keys from datetime values, causing pagination to error once a non-zero cursor is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — The gate uses request.user.is_superuser (the account flag) instead of is_active_superuser(request), granting advanced mode to superuser accounts without an active elevated superuser session; additionally, the branch's stated goal of enabling access to data beyond normal pagination bounds via a hidden query parameter is a bypass-shaped design that should not be merged (a real reverse-pagination need belongs in the cursor protocol, not a superuser-only escape hatch)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a hidden query-parameter gate (`optimized_pagination=true`) in `organization_auditlogs.py` and enables an alternate paginator with an `enable_advanced_features=True` flag for `request.user.is_superuser` / `has_global_access`. The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` explicitly documents/implements “negative offset” behavior intended to go “beyond normal pagination bounds”. That is a concrete, diff-grounded design/architecture/security concern (special admin-only escape hatch rather than part of the cursor protocol). However, the specific claim that it must use `is_active_superuser(request)` instead of `request.user.is_superuser` is not verifiable from the diff alone (we can see `is_superuser` is used, but not what the project’s required superuser-session policy is).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:820 — No tests cover OptimizedCursorPaginator, the new endpoint branch, or the changed negative-offset handling in BasePaginator.get_result; a single test requesting one page through the new path would have caught the failures

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new, branchy behavior (a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` class, a new endpoint branch gated by `optimized_pagination`/admin checks, and altered offset handling in `BasePaginator.get_result`), but the diff itself contains no corresponding test additions. While we can’t prove from the diff that *no* existing tests cover these paths, it’s a specific, diff-grounded review concern that these new code paths/edge cases may be untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:67 — optimized_pagination is a new query parameter on a public, documented endpoint but is not added to the endpoint's schema/parameters or docs, and its behavior differs per caller (silently ignored for non-admins)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new query parameter gate in `organization_auditlogs.py` (`use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"`) and then conditionally uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` only when `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` is true. For non-admin callers, the parameter is effectively ignored and the endpoint silently falls back to `DateTimePaginator`. The claim about missing schema/docs for a public documented endpoint is not verifiable from this diff alone, but the new undocumented/implicit behavior switch based on caller privileges is real and review-relevant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:820 — The docstring and PR description claim performance optimizations (optimized query path for large datasets, without full dataset scanning), but get_result is a near-verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result issuing the same query; there is no performance change and the class is duplicated code with a misleading name

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` is largely a copy of existing paginator logic and still slices the queryset (`list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`) in essentially the same way, with the main added behavior being optional negative-offset slicing when `enable_advanced_features` is set. The docstring/comments claim broader “performance optimizations” and an “optimized query path for large datasets,” which is not concretely demonstrated by any materially different query strategy beyond that negative-offset branch. This makes the name/docstring potentially misleading and introduces duplicated pagination code, but it’s not a directly verifiable correctness defect solely from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26 — The added comment says negative offsets are now allowed as a performance optimization, but no code changed here (int(offset) already accepted negatives) and negative offsets are not supported downstream; the comment documents behavior that does not exist

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `src/sentry/utils/cursors.py` only adds a comment; while it’s true `int(offset)` already accepted negatives, the finding’s claim that “negative offsets are not supported downstream” is contradicted by this PR: `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` changes offset handling (e.g., allowing `offset` to pass through when `cursor.is_prev`) and adds `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, which explicitly slices with a negative `cursor.offset` when `enable_advanced_features` is set. Whether Django actually supports negative queryset slicing isn’t verifiable from the diff alone, but the PR clearly does add downstream logic to attempt/support it, so the finding as stated is false.
